challenges.lessonTitle: What Python Is and How Programs Run
challenges.title: Python Program Execution
challenges.question: What is the main role of Python when a program runs?

options.text: It follows saved instructions step by step.
It guesses what the developer wanted.

challenges.explanation: Python executes the instructions written in a file. It does not infer missing logic or automatically fix incorrect code.

challenges.title: Running a Python File
challenges.question: Which action runs a saved Python file from the terminal?

options.text: Use python followed by the file name.
Put print before the file name.

challenges.explanation: A Python file runs when you ask Python to execute that saved file, usually with python and the file name.

challenges.lessonTitle: Printing Text, Numbers, and Multiple Values
challenges.title: Printing Multiple Values
challenges.question: What does print("XP:", 100) display?
challenges.explanation: print() can display multiple values in one line. Python separates comma-separated values with spaces in the output.

challenges.title: Readable Python Code
challenges.question: What is the purpose of a comment in Python code?

options.text: To explain code for humans reading it.

challenges.explanation: Comments are ignored by Python and are used to make code easier for people to understand.

challenges.title: Console Greeting Output
challenges.question: What should a simple console greeting program do?

options.text: Print a clear greeting message in the terminal.
Hide all output from the user.

challenges.explanation: A console greeting program practices basic output by showing a readable message in the terminal.

challenges.title: Variables
challenges.question: What is a variable in Python?

options.text: A name that refers to a value.
A file that always stores code.

challenges.explanation: A variable gives a useful name to a value so the program can use it later.

challenges.title: Integer and Float Values
challenges.question: Which value is a float in Python?
challenges.explanation: A float is a number with a decimal point, such as 3.14.

challenges.title: Basic Value Types
challenges.question: Which value is a Boolean?
challenges.explanation: Boolean values are True and False. They are often used for decisions.

challenges.title: Type Conversion
challenges.question: Why might you convert "100" with int("100")?

options.text: To turn text into a number for calculations.
To turn a number into a comment.
To make the value print twice.

challenges.explanation: Input-like values often start as text, so converting them lets Python do numeric work.

challenges.title: Updating Values
challenges.question: What does score += 10 do?

options.text: Adds 10 to score and stores the result.

challenges.explanation: The += operator updates a variable by adding a value to its current value.

challenges.title: Boolean Decisions
challenges.question: What is the result of a comparison such as score >= 70?

options.text: A Boolean value: True or False

challenges.explanation: Comparison expressions evaluate to Boolean values, which are commonly used by if statements.

challenges.title: if Statements
challenges.question: When does the indented block under an if statement run?

options.text: Only when a comment is present.

challenges.explanation: An if block runs only when its condition evaluates to True.

challenges.title: else Branches
challenges.question: What does an else block provide?

options.text: A path to run when the if condition is False.
A second file for Python to run.

challenges.explanation: else handles the alternative path when the if condition does not pass.

challenges.title: Multiple Conditions
challenges.question: Why use elif in a conditional chain?

options.text: To check another condition after the first if.

challenges.explanation: elif lets a program choose among multiple possible conditions in order.

challenges.title: Guard Clauses
challenges.question: What is one benefit of a guard clause?

options.text: It handles an early case so the main logic stays clearer.
It makes every condition run twice.
It removes the need for Boolean values.
It changes a list into a tuple.

challenges.explanation: A guard clause can handle a special case early and reduce deeply nested code.

challenges.title: Access Rules
challenges.question: What should an access gate program check first?

options.text: The conditions that decide whether access is allowed.
The color of the terminal window.
The number of comments in the file.
Whether the file name is short.

challenges.explanation: An access gate is built from clear conditions that decide whether a user can continue.

challenges.title: while Loops
challenges.question: When does a while loop continue repeating?
challenges.explanation: A while loop repeats as long as its condition evaluates to True.

challenges.title: range() Loops
challenges.question: When is for item in range(3) useful?

options.text: When you want a known number of repeats.
When you want to stop Python from running.
When you need to create a comment.
When a value must be None.

challenges.explanation: range() is helpful when the number of loop repeats is known ahead of time.

challenges.title: Looping Through Items
challenges.question: What does a for loop do when used with a list?

options.text: It visits each item so the code can process it.
It turns every item into a file.
It deletes the list before reading it.
It changes the list name into a number.

challenges.explanation: Looping through a collection lets one block of code handle each stored item.

challenges.title: Loop Control
challenges.question: What does break do inside a loop?

options.text: It skips only the current iteration.
It converts a string to an integer.

challenges.explanation: break exits the loop immediately, before the normal loop condition would stop it.

challenges.title: Counting Repeated Progress
challenges.question: What programming idea is most useful for a training counter?

options.text: A loop that repeats for each round.
A comment that runs as code.
A file path stored as True.

challenges.explanation: A counter often uses a loop to repeat work and update progress over several rounds.

challenges.title: Lists
challenges.question: What does it mean that a list is mutable?

options.text: Its contents can be changed after creation.
It can only store one value.

challenges.explanation: Lists are mutable, so you can add, remove, or update their items.

challenges.title: Tuples
challenges.question: When is a tuple a good choice?

options.text: When a small ordered record should not change.
When every item must be deleted often.
When keys are required for lookup.
When duplicate values must be removed.

challenges.explanation: Tuples are useful for ordered data that should stay fixed.

challenges.title: Dictionaries
challenges.question: How does a dictionary store data?

options.text: Only as unique values without labels.

challenges.explanation: A dictionary uses meaningful keys to find related values.

challenges.title: Sets
challenges.question: What is a key feature of a set?

options.text: It stores each value only once.
It keeps duplicate values in order.

challenges.explanation: Sets keep unique values, which makes them useful for removing duplicates or checking membership.

challenges.title: Data Structure Choice
challenges.question: Which choice is best when you need named fields like name and score?
challenges.explanation: A dictionary is useful when values should be accessed by meaningful keys.

challenges.title: Functions
challenges.question: Why define a function?

options.text: To give reusable code a clear name.
To force all values to be strings.

challenges.explanation: A function packages reusable logic under a name so it can be called when needed.

challenges.title: Parameters and Arguments
challenges.question: What does a parameter let a function do?

options.text: Accept input values when it is called.
Skip all code inside the function.

challenges.explanation: Parameters make functions flexible by letting callers provide values.

challenges.title: Return Values
challenges.question: What does return do in a function?

options.text: Sends a value back to the caller.
Always prints a value to the terminal.

challenges.explanation: return gives a result back to the code that called the function.

challenges.title: Scope
challenges.question: What is a local variable?

options.text: A variable created inside a function.
A variable that must be stored in a file.
A value that is always True.

challenges.explanation: A local variable exists inside the function where it is created.

challenges.title: Default Arguments
challenges.question: What is the purpose of a default argument?

options.text: To provide a value when the caller does not pass one.
To prevent a function from being called.

challenges.explanation: A default argument makes common calls simpler while still allowing a custom value.

challenges.title: String Slicing
challenges.question: What does slicing a string let you do?
challenges.explanation: Slicing uses positions to take a smaller piece from a string.

challenges.title: String Methods
challenges.question: What does name.strip() commonly do?

options.text: Removes extra whitespace from the ends.
Turns the string into a list of files.

challenges.explanation: strip() is commonly used to clean text by removing leading and trailing whitespace.

challenges.title: Checking Text
challenges.question: Which expression checks whether text contains @?
challenges.explanation: The in operator checks whether one string appears inside another string.

challenges.title: Split and Join
challenges.question: What does split() do to text?

options.text: Combines a list into one string.
Turns text into True or False.

challenges.explanation: split() breaks a string into pieces, often using whitespace or a chosen separator.

challenges.title: Username Formatting
challenges.question: Why should a username formatter clean text before saving it?

options.text: To make usernames consistent and predictable.
To make every username a number.

challenges.explanation: Cleaning text helps produce consistent usernames from different user inputs.

challenges.title: Opening Files Safely
challenges.question: Why is with open(...) useful when working with files?

options.text: It closes the file automatically after the block.
It prevents all errors in the file.
It turns file text into a Boolean.
It deletes the file after reading.

challenges.explanation: The with block manages the file and closes it when the block is done.

challenges.title: Reading Files
challenges.question: What does reading a file allow a program to do?

options.text: Load saved text from outside the program.
Turn every line into a comment.

challenges.explanation: Reading files lets a program use information that was saved outside the running code.

challenges.title: Writing Files
challenges.question: What is the difference between writing and appending?

options.text: Writing can replace content; appending adds to the end.
Appending always deletes the file first.
They are names for the same comment.

challenges.explanation: Writing can create or replace content, while appending keeps existing content and adds more.

challenges.title: CSV-Style Text
challenges.question: How does CSV-style text commonly store fields?

options.text: By separating values with commas or another delimiter.

challenges.explanation: CSV-style data stores table-like values by separating fields with a delimiter such as a comma.

challenges.title: Saving Progress
challenges.question: Why might a program save progress to a file?

options.text: So progress can be loaded again later.
So every line becomes a number.

challenges.explanation: Saving progress lets a program keep information between runs.

challenges.title: Exceptions
challenges.question: What does an exception usually mean?

options.text: Python cannot continue safely with the current operation.
A variable changed into a file.

challenges.explanation: An exception signals that something went wrong and Python cannot safely continue that operation.

challenges.title: Handling Expected Failure
challenges.question: What is the role of an except block?

options.text: To handle an error raised in the try block.
To run before the try block.
To create a new Python type.

challenges.explanation: except lets a program respond to expected errors without crashing immediately.

challenges.title: else and finally
challenges.question: When does the finally block run?

options.text: After try/except handling, whether an error happened or not.
Only before the try block starts.
Only when a file has no text.
Only when a variable is a string.

challenges.explanation: finally is used for cleanup code that should run whether the try block succeeds or fails.

challenges.title: Raising Errors
challenges.question: Why might a function raise an error on purpose?

options.text: To turn every value into text.

challenges.explanation: Raising an error intentionally can make bad input clear before the program continues.

challenges.title: Safe Number Parsing
challenges.question: What should a safe number parser do with invalid text?

options.text: Handle it without crashing and give useful feedback.
Always treat it as the number 100.

challenges.explanation: A safe parser handles invalid input gracefully instead of letting the program crash without context.
